1.title: Know housekeeping work
1.intro: Housekeeping keeps homes, hotels and care spaces clean, tidy and ready. Start with the areas, tasks and words.
pts: Name areas: bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, living space, laundry.
Describe daily, weekly and deep-clean tasks.
Explain the difference between cleaning, sanitising and disinfecting.
List words: linen, turnover, checklist, supplies cart, stain.
1.ex: A guest room turnover: strip bed, empty bins, clean bathroom, dust, vacuum, make bed, restock, final check. Each step is on one list.
1.act: Write a room-by-room task list for one real room and time each task.
1.std: Task: list housekeeping tasks. Condition: one real room. Standard: all areas covered and times written.

2.title: Use tools and products safely
2.intro: The right tool and product make work faster and safer. The wrong mix can harm you.
pts: Name basic tools: cloths, mop, vacuum, scrub brush, bucket, gloves.
Read a product label and a safety data sheet for hazards and use.
Check that you never mix bleach with ammonia or acid cleaners.
Apply colour-coded cloths to avoid spreading germs.
2.ex: Red cloths for bathroom, blue for glass, green for kitchen. Bleach is used alone, diluted by the label, with gloves and fresh air.
2.act: Read the label of three products at home and write the hazard, use and first aid.
2.std: Task: use products safely. Condition: three real labels. Standard: hazard, use and first aid recorded correctly for each.

3.title: Follow the rules in Canada
3.intro: Workplace safety, hazard labels and employment rules apply. Check with the local authority.
pts: Explain that hazardous products use standard labels and safety data sheets; read them before use.
Describe workplace safety training that employers must give; check your province.
Check employment standards for pay, breaks and overtime; they differ by province.
Apply privacy and trust: never take or share anything you see in a client's home.
3.ex: Rules table row: Hazard training | provincial workplace safety body | complete before using strong products | before first shift | certificate kept.
3.act: Make a rules table covering safety training, labels, pay rules and privacy, with official pages.
3.std: Task: map the rules. Condition: official pages only. Standard: each row has an enforcer, an action and a checked date.

4.title: Clean to a standard
4.intro: Standards turn good intentions into repeatable results.
pts: Apply the order: top to bottom, back to front, dry to wet.
Build a room standard with photos of done and not done.
Check each room with a checklist before you leave.
Record time per room to improve planning.
4.ex: Bathroom standard: mirror streak-free, tap shiny, no hair in drain, floor dry, supplies stocked. Photo of the finished room is saved.
4.act: Clean one room twice. The second time use your checklist and compare time and result.
4.std: Task: clean a room to a standard. Condition: written checklist. Standard: every item passed and second run is faster or better.

5.title: Laundry, linen and special surfaces
5.intro: Different materials need different care. Mistakes cost money.
pts: Apply care labels for washing, heat and drying.
Compare surfaces: wood, stone, glass, steel, carpet; choose safe products.
Handle stains: act early, test a hidden spot, work from outside in.
Check bed linen standards: clean, dry, undamaged, folded the same way.
5.ex: A red wine stain on carpet: blot, do not rub, use cool water and a mild cleaner after a hidden-spot test.
5.act: Test two stain methods on cloth scraps and write which worked and why.
5.std: Task: remove a stain. Condition: scrap test. Standard: hidden-spot test done first and method recorded.

6.title: Price your time and plan jobs
6.intro: Clients pay for results, but you must cover time, travel and supplies.
pts: Compute cost per job: time, travel, supplies, insurance, tax set-aside.
Compare hourly and fixed prices and explain which suits each job.
Build a weekly plan with travel time and rest.
Evaluate which jobs pay well for the time and which do not.
6.ex: Fixed price 120 for a 3-hour home, supplies 8, travel 6. Margin 106. If fixed costs are 300 a month, break-even is about 3 jobs. Teaching numbers only.
6.act: Build a cost sheet and a price list for three job types.
6.std: Task: price a job. Condition: all costs counted. Standard: margin and break-even correct and shown with units.

7.title: Health, trust and clients
7.intro: You work in private spaces. Safety, honesty and respect build repeat work.
pts: Apply body safety: lift well, kneel with padding, take breaks, protect hands.
Check keys and codes: store safely and never copy without permission.
Write a service agreement: tasks, hours, access, cancellations, breakage.
Handle a damage case: stop, tell the client, photo, written note.
7.ex: A vase breaks. Housekeeper stops, tells the client at once, takes a photo, writes what happened. Honesty keeps the client.
7.act: Write an agreement, a key-handling rule and a damage report form.
7.std: Task: protect trust. Condition: practice case. Standard: agreement has tasks and access; damage form completed honestly.

8.title: Run the service for real
8.intro: Now run your housekeeping service with real clients, quality checks and a plan.
pts: Run a 60-day pilot with a stop rule agreed in advance.
Review weekly: jobs, time per job, quality score, complaints.
Create a 12-month plan with insurance, supplies and growth.
Lead others: train a helper using your standards and photos.
8.ex: Stop rule: if fewer than 15 jobs in 60 days, stop and write lessons. Result: 24 jobs and 3 repeat clients; add a part-time helper.
8.act: Run the pilot, write the review and present your plan to three people.
8.std: Task: run a housekeeping pilot. Condition: 60 days, real clients. Standard: results compared with the stop rule and safety training confirmed.

quiz: What is the cleaning order?
Top to bottom, back to front, dry to wet.
Why use colour-coded cloths?
To avoid spreading germs between areas.
What must you never mix?
Bleach with ammonia or acid cleaners.
Where do you find product hazards?
The label and the safety data sheet.
What do you do before using a stain remover?
Test it on a hidden spot.
What should a service agreement include?
Tasks, hours, access, cancellations and breakage.
How should you store client keys?
Safely, labelled by code, never copied without permission.
What do you do if you break something?
Stop, tell the client, take a photo and write a note.
How do you find break-even jobs?
Fixed cost divided by margin per job.
Who sets pay and break rules?
The province; check employment standards.
